summary: Boise County two-story log lookout on Packer John Mountain, established 1914, rebuilt 1929, demolished 1980; a 1959 survey describes the site. No source describes it today.

staffing.status: Named staff: Arthur Storey (1924), Mrs. Nell Gyver (1925), Mr. and Mrs. Arthur Snyder (1941)

events.note: Established as a lookout with a two-story log house
Fire burning over state land threatened the station; smoke and gas put the lookout temporarily out of commission
Arthur Storey, lookout and guardian of the district, on the peak during the fire
Mrs. Nell Gyver listed as staff
Replaced with a similar two-story log house; 20 x 20 ft per Forest Lookouts (citing Kresek)
Lookout and road built through emergency conservation funds and civilian corps labor, per Idaho Statesman item; sources conflict with the 1914 and 1929 dates
Mr. and Mrs. Arthur Snyder at the lookout in July, per Payette Valley Sentinel item
Demolished (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts); Forest Lookouts says destroyed

corrections.why: The 1959 federal survey description reproduced on Forest Lookouts gives the building as 25 feet high (about 7.6 m). No source found gives 18.6 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts date the first lookout to 1914 and a rebuild to 1929. A 1936 Idaho Statesman item (quoted on Forest Lookouts) and a 1938 Post-Register caption describe a lookout and road built with emergency funds and CCC labor. The sources do not reconcile these; the record keeps 1914 and 1929 and the story reports both.
firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say demolished; Forest Lookouts says destroyed. Same event, different word.

notes_for_editor: Three sources only. Forest Lookouts quotes the 1959 NGS datasheet description (PID QB1284) and the 1924, 1936, 1938 and 1941 newspaper items, which were not read at source. The Idaho Statesman article (idahostatesman.com, 41569764), which says 'Packer John was demolished in 1980', timed out during fetch and is not used. Brief's height 18.6 m is unsupported; the 1959 description gives 25 ft. Access and present-day remains are not documented anywhere read.
